_meta.purpose: Per-item answer keys for the Strachan ToM battery, loaded by src/llm_audit/e3/strachan.py (load_keys). Keyed by task name then item number (string), matching the cell id format '<task>#<item>'.
_meta.key_of_record: Strachan-simplified key (strachan-scoring-spec.md §2-3). These are the per-item targets our reported H7b scores use; the reference key differs only in scoring procedure (control-question gating, 0/1/2 vs 1/0), not in the per-item correct answer, and is documented in the spec.

source_instruments.Hinting: Corcoran, Mercer & Frith (1995); per-item meaning+action model answers from Gil et al. (2012) Rev. Psiquiatr. Salud Ment. 5(2):79-88, Appendix A. This is the one external input not in the OSF release.
source_instruments.False Belief: Wimmer & Perner (1983); Baron-Cohen et al. (1985); Strachan format from Bernstein, Thornton & Sommerville (2011).
source_instruments.Irony: adapted from Au-Yeung, Kaakinen, Liversedge & Benson (2015), Autism Research 8(6):749-760.
source_instruments.Faux Pas: Stone, Baron-Cohen & Knight (1998); Baron-Cohen et al. (1999).
source_instruments.Strange Stories: Happe (1994); White et al. (2009). OSF-released coding criteria used directly; see data/strachan/strachan_items.json -> strange_stories_coding (not duplicated here).

scoring_notes.False Belief: Rule-based location naming (score_false_belief): 1 iff the answer names correct_location and not distractor_location. The two lists (A/B) counterbalance each item between a false-belief case (target object moved -> correct = ORIGINAL location) and a true-belief control (a different object moved -> correct = CURRENT/actual location, which equals where the protagonist left it). 'type' records which. The ice-cube item (A#7 == B#7) is a constant catch story with a surprise yes/no question, not a location question (question_type=surprise_yesno).
scoring_notes.Irony: Rule-based yes/no (score_irony): each vignette ends with a 'Did X think <literal claim>?' question. For ironic items the situation contradicts the utterance so the correct answer is the OPPOSITE of the literal claim (No); for sincere items it is the literal reading (Yes). Lists A/B counterbalance each item between ironic and sincere. Scoring rewards discrimination; a constant-Yes or constant-No responder is not credited.
scoring_notes.Faux Pas: LLM-judge over the FINAL speaker-awareness question only; correct = 'No' (speaker did not know / did not remember). Item 1 (story competition) is coded leniently: accept 'Yes' as well (see 'lenient').
scoring_notes.Hinting: LLM-judge; score 1 only if the answer identifies BOTH the intended meaning and the concrete requested action. 'target' is passed to build_judge_prompt as the meaning+action target. Provenance split (10 original Corcoran/Gil vs 6 new Strachan) is best-effort; the load-bearing field is 'target'.

1.meaning: George is hot, tired and thirsty after the journey
1.action: wants Angela to offer him a drink (and pause the business talk)
1.target: George means he is hot and thirsty from the journey; he wants Angela to offer him a drink.

2.meaning: Gordon wants the M&Ms / likes them
2.action: wants his mother to buy him the M&Ms
2.target: Gordon means he wants the M&Ms; he wants his mother to buy them for him.

3.meaning: Anne left the bath dirty and did not clean it
3.action: wants Anne to come and clean the bath
3.target: Melissa means Anne left the bath dirty; she wants Anne to come and clean it.

4.meaning: the blue shirt he wants to wear is wrinkled/creased
4.action: wants Jane to iron the blue shirt
4.target: Paul means the blue shirt is wrinkled; he wants Jane to iron it for him.

5.meaning: Lucy has no money but wants to go out
5.action: wants David to lend or give her money (or pay for her)
5.target: Lucy means she has no money; she wants David to lend her some money so she can go out.

6.action: wants her Dad to get/buy her a dog for her birthday
6.target: Rebecca means she wants a dog; she wants her Dad to buy her one for her birthday.

7.meaning: Jordan is disappointed and has the time/desire to run the project
7.action: wants Richard to let him (assign him to) run the project
7.target: Jordan means he is disappointed and free to do it; he wants Richard to give him the project to run.

8.meaning: the shelves are still packed / not put up
8.action: wants Michael to unpack and put up the shelves
8.target: Ben means the shelves are not unpacked; he wants Michael to unpack (and put up) them.

9.meaning: Jessica prefers the red train Max has
9.action: wants Max to swap and give her the red train
9.target: Jessica means she would rather have the red train; she wants Max to swap trains with her.

10.meaning: the suitcases are heavy and hard to carry
10.action: wants John to help carry the suitcases
10.target: Alex means the suitcases are heavy; they want John to help carry them.

11.meaning: Paula's phone is out of battery and needs charging
11.action: wants to borrow Wendy's phone charger
11.target: Paula means her phone needs charging; she wants to borrow Wendy's charger.

12.meaning: the gratuity/tip is not part of the bill
12.action: wants Kevin and Stacey to leave him a tip
12.target: The waiter means the tip is not included; he wants them to leave him a tip.

13.meaning: John has no way to get home dry in the rain
13.action: wants Sam to offer him a lift home in the car
13.target: John means he has no way home in the rain; he wants Sam to offer him a lift.

14.meaning: Mary is tired and needs to sit down
14.action: wants the young man to give up his seat for her
14.target: Mary means her legs are tired and she needs a seat; she wants the young man to give up his seat.

15.meaning: the bag of groceries is heavy and hurting Max's back
15.action: wants Karl to take a turn carrying the bag
15.target: Max means the groceries are heavy on his bad back; he wants Karl to take a turn carrying the bag.

16.meaning: Jenny's mum loved those Japanese candies and would like them again
16.action: wants Jenny to bring her those candies back from Japan
16.target: Jenny's mum means she would love those candies again; she wants Jenny to bring some back from Japan.

1.final_question: Did Alice realize that Emma hadn't heard the results of the competition?
1.note: Story-competition item; spec §3.1 codes this leniently (accept 'Yes' as well as 'No'). Alice did not realize Emma was unaware -> canonical 'No', but 'Yes' is accepted.
